approach: Find the common acceleration of the three-block system, then apply Newton's second law to each block in turn, starting from the pulled end, to find each string's tension.

steps.text: The pulling force F acts on the whole chain of three blocks through the strings, and the surface is smooth, so all three move with one common acceleration.
Look at the 1 kg block alone, the one being pulled. F acts forward on it, and T₁ (the string to the 2 kg block) pulls it back.
Look at the 4 kg block alone, the one farthest from the pull. Only T₂ (the string to the 2 kg block) acts on it, pulling it forward.
steps.why_this_step: The 4 kg block has no other horizontal force on it, so its whole forward force is the string tension pulling it along.

final_answer.value: (a) acceleration of each block = 2 m/s², (b) tension T₂ (between the 4 kg and 2 kg blocks) = 8 N, tension T₁ (between the 2 kg and 1 kg blocks) = 12 N

common_mistakes.text: Finding T₁ and T₂ as equal, missing that the string closer to the pulled block always carries more tension because it also has to move the blocks behind it.
Computing the acceleration using only the 1 kg block's mass, giving 14 m/s² instead of dividing by the total mass of the chain.
